evidence.behavior: main hides console, gates on evasion.Suspicious, creates and shuffles concurrent collectors, waits for them, collects screenshot, stages app/wallet/game/device data, finalizes archive and calls EncryptAndSend
collectBrowserRaw extracts DPAPI v10 key, starts pipe session for v20 app-bound key, then collectProfileRaw stages keys, Local State, Cookies, Login Data, Web Data and History

CreatePipeSession decrypts embedded helper, finds browser PIDs or creates hidden suspended headless browser (flags 0x08000004), reflectively injects helper using NT allocate/write/protect/thread APIs, then receives key and locked-file results on a named pipe
searchEncryptedTokens obtains browser master key, searches Discord encrypted-token prefix, Base64 decodes, AES-GCM decrypts and validates token syntax before staging results
wallet collector locates desktop wallets and recursively copies wallet directories using locked-file reads into CryptoData
EncryptAndSend derives session transport key, creates AES-GCM cipher, random nonce and HMAC, seals with certificate context, TLS dials configured 103.249.200.71:9090 and writes encrypted archive
Checks PEB BeingDebugged and NtGlobalFlag at offset 0xbc with mask 0x70; also calls resource, uptime, analysis-process and VM-registry checks; main returns on suspicious result

samples.missing_context: Delivery and actual victim execution are unknown. The explicit credential acquisition, browser injection and outbound archive chain establish hostile behavior without runtime success.

evidence.behavior: Entry transfers into .themida through scattered stack and jump dispatch. Original main at 0x1400052a0 also jumps into protected code at 0x14058bc5e. Offline trace crosses the dispatcher into original routines.
Loads win32u.dll with user32.dll fallback, resolves NtUserSetWindowsHookEx and NtUserUnhookWindowsHookEx and stores function pointers

Keyboard callback accepts action notifications, decodes KEYDOWN/KEYUP/SYSKEYDOWN/SYSKEYUP and virtual-key codes, prints virtual key, scan code, time and flags to C++ console stream, then forwards hook-chain event
Mouse callback prints button/wheel events, coordinates, time and flags; mouse-move spam is skipped

Protected-main emulation reaches reading ntdll.dll from disk, in-memory PE loading, export lookup of NtRaiseHardError and an error-report path. This does not establish ntdll unhooking, process injection, C2 or destructive hard-error use.

samples.verdict_balance: Global input recording plus unsigned, heavily protected packaging and analysis-environment probes tip the incident-triage judgment toward malicious. Visible console diagnostics, Chinese initialization/error text and orderly hook forwarding also fit an input-hook demonstration. Neither keylogging capability nor Themida alone establishes intent; an authorized testing/instrumentation context could change this judgment.
samples.missing_context: User consent, intended testing role, launch provenance and authorization are unavailable. No covert log file, persistence, credential extraction or network exfiltration was established. Protected control flow was only partially recovered; mock-dependent emulation is not proof of runtime success.

decoded_helper.classifier_limit: Recovered DLL alone remains below calibrated alert threshold; malicious role is established by the decoded-helper-to-browser-injection chain in its parent. It is not an archive member and the scanner did not automatically recover this XOR layer.

coverage_review.retained_attacks: No pre-existing hostile or suspicious finding was lost on either original sample. The first sample gains five new hostile composites plus an existing multi-app credential composite. The second gains two suspicious behaviors, with no invented hostile subtype.

losses.resolution: Same matcher, scope, confidence and managed-version exclusion moved to micro-behaviors/communications/ip/endpoint at notable. Exact consumers and CrystalX ancestor-directory exclusion population retained via its existing exception group.

Original Go matches were quotaNonPagedPoolUsage and quotaPeakNonPagedPoolUsage field names, not allocation flags. New usage-field reference preserves that observation. Whole-token executable pool enums retained; NX/session enum references preserved separately under heap allocation. No exact consumers exist. Real upstream ReactOS NTFS allocation code remains positive.

Generic OR aggregate no longer emitted in the full scan after constituent AES/RSA package references became notable. Its rule is unchanged and test-rules still matches it. Both underlying package observations remain, at increased criticality; no cryptographic or attack behavior was removed.

coverage_review.remaining_disagreement: Second original and recovered helper remain below the calibrated classifier alert grid despite suspicious input capture/protection and the parent-established helper role. First original now alerts at level 25. Do not add duplicate or unsupported hostile rules to force either miss.
tool_limitations: Atomscan model bundle v18.18 warns that its feature spec is v18 while the extractor produces v19; no retraining was attempted.

test-rules reports only native symbols on the first PE and misses recovered Go call predicates, whereas cleave facts exposes 71977 symbol/call records and full atomscan correctly fires all new Go composites. Composite precision diagnostics were still obtained.
